result:
**Round 2 verdict: FAIL.** 22 of 24 checks pass, but the video drifts out of sync with the sound during playback, which is the main thing FB-16 asks for. I tested everything myself in a fresh browser session with no login.

**What fails**
- **R3-V1, video/audio sync.** The target is median drift Γëñ 0.05 s and max Γëñ 0.1 s. I ran the 0ΓÇô6 / 8ΓÇô12 s layout plus a music clip 10 times in one page load. 5 runs failed (1, 4, 6, 7, 9), with max drift 0.127ΓÇô0.149 s; runs 1 and 7 also failed the median (0.065 and 0.076 s).
- **R2-V3, playback after edits.** The clip offsets after trim, split and Delete Time are exactly right. But playback drift failed in 2 of 3 runs (median up to 0.081 s, max 0.154 s).
- **Cause (C-R2-01, High).** `ArrangementVideoDock.tsx:103ΓÇô111` fires a new seek every ~250 ms even while the previous seek hasn't finished. Each seek also aims ahead of the playhead by a learned "lead" that overshoots. The video then stays stuck mid-seek for up to 1.3 s, and the picture freezes for up to 800 ms.
- **Test environment.** This was the headless browser, where video seeking may be slower than in real Chrome. The repeated-seek behaviour is in the code, though. After a fix, the Tech Lead should confirm sync in real Chrome.
- **C-R2-02 (Low).** On Play, the video starts before the sound does. On the very first Play it ran 0.22 s ahead. This falls inside the excluded first 300 ms, so it doesn't fail any check.

**What passes**
- **Build checks:** 557/557 tests, typecheck clean, build OK, lint 0 errors. The 4 protected files are unchanged, and only the allowed files were touched.
- **Premium login is not bypassed:**
  - Studio token request without login ΓåÆ 401; with a fake token ΓåÆ 500 and no token issued.
  - `/studio/middle-east` ΓåÆ "Sign in required", with no stem or R2 requests.
  - Imported videos never leave the browser; only local `blob:` URLs are used.
- **Round-1 fixes:**
  - 5 quick Play/Pause pairs at 20.000 ΓåÆ exactly 20.000.
  - The playhead never moves backwards.
  - Editing while playing hands the audio over with 0 ms step.
  - The page no longer scrolls at either screen size.
  - The status line wraps instead of being cut off.
  - Undo of Delete Time while playing keeps the playhead where it is.
- **Video import:**
  - Picker and drag-and-drop place clips one after another.
  - Undo/Redo brings back the same clip.
  - Audio, PDF and broken files are all rejected without changing history.
  - A `.mov` with no file type is still accepted.
  - MP4 and MOV work in this browser, so they're verified rather than left to real Chrome.
- **Video sound and export:**
  - Muting the video lane gives exact silence; unmuting is audible immediately, with no restart.
  - Solo on another lane silences the video's sound.
  - The exported WAV matches my own decode of the test file to within 5.96e-8, with beeps exactly at 2.5ΓÇª6.5 s.
  - A video with no sound exports a correct silent WAV, and the export dialog says the video has no sound.
- **Playhead, Space and Home:**
  - Dragging the playhead while playing re-schedules audio 12 times plus once on release; the limit is 15. The drag adds no undo entry.
  - Arrow keys move the playhead ┬▒0.1 s.
  - Home returns to 0 and does nothing inside a text box.
  - Real Space presses never double the sounds and leave the video paused/playing in step with the transport.
- **Round-1 regressions** re-run with a video clip present all pass.
- **Screenshots:** at both screen sizes the video preview fits without overlap, and the sound library scrolls at 1280├ù720.

To repeat the prototype test (R2-V0), I copied the prototype into my own `c-round-2/proto/` folder, because the browser can only open local files from there. All my test scripts and saved results are in that same `c-round-2` folder.

Files are in `C:\Apps\czaba-project\tmp\studio-real-loop\`:
- c-round-2.md
- c-round-2.json
- c-round-2/

Several connected services (Atlassian, Gmail, Google Calendar/Drive, Microsoft 365, Similarweb, Klaviyo, Amplitude, Slack) need authorizing in your claude.ai connector settings or via `/mcp`. They weren't needed for this check.
